decisions.decision: Arrows, tyre-column rename and naming rule ship together as one roadmap.
decisions.why: User chose to keep MAG-59 whole rather than split the rename into its own ticket.

decisions.decision: Store day-over-day deltas in new columns, computed from the row the loop built one step earlier. LAG rejected.
decisions.why: Postgres runs window functions before DISTINCT ON, so LAG would read each vehicle's whole history on a page load and lose the one-row read.

decisions.decision: All three tiles show direction. Only Efficiency carries a good/bad colour; Distance and Battery are neutral.
decisions.why: Driving more or using more charge is neither good nor bad, so a green arrow would praise a neutral fact.

decisions.decision: Delta columns are named _delta_calc, including the four renamed tyre columns.
decisions.why: One naming rule across the whole database, so a later reader cannot mistake a delta for the day's own figure.

decisions.decision: The naming rule goes in ai/go-conventions.md and is enforced by a make guard.
decisions.why: A guard is a deterministic signal, so the mistake fails fast instead of costing a human review round.

decisions.decision: Tier order is guard first, then analytics, then gateway.
decisions.why: Gateway cannot read columns analytics has not stored. Guard first matches the owner's stated preference and its baseline keeps make check green.

decisions.decision: Guard baseline covers all ten pre-existing _calc names, not only the four tyre ones.
decisions.why: A repo-wide grep found ten columns across analytics and charging. The roadmap's four-name claim was wrong and is corrected.

decisions.decision: The tier 2 backfill joins on metric_date - 1, not on the previous stored row.
decisions.why: Same rule the tyre-pressure backfill used. After a gap the historical value stays NULL.
